To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) is expressed in the ciliary epithelium (CE), that it is involved in the regulation of aqueous humor outflow, and that its activity is decreased in the CE of patients with POAG.
soluble and membrane guanyl cyclases (GCs), the enzymes that produce cGMP, are expressed in the eye and regulate IOP, and that soluble and membrane GCs may play a role in the pathogenesis of POAG.

soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) and natriuretic receptor-A (NPR-A) are expressed in the trabecular meshwork, and that sGC and NPR-A are down-regulated in POAG patients, and that sGCa and NPR-A may be useful biomarkers of glaucoma and potential therapeutic targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
understanding the role of cGMP in the regulation of aqueous humor (AH) formation, the major component of IOP regulation.
the role of cGMP and the guanylate cyclase (GC) system in the regulation of aqueous humor (AH) formation and outflow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of NO and NP signaling pathways in IOP regulation is still unclear.
soluble and membrane guanyl cyclases are key players in the pathophysiological regulation of IOP.
the role of NO- and NP-activated GCs in the regulation of the aqueous humor outflow and in the pathogenesis of POAG is not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NO- and NP-activated guanylatecyclases regulate IOP, and that NO- and/or NP-cGMP signaling are altered in glaucomatous optic nerve heads.

NO and natriuretic peptides (NPs) are important regulators of IOP and their receptors, soluble (s) guanylate cyclase (sGC) and natriurete peptide receptors (NPRs), respectively, are potential drug targets for the management of glaucoma and that the sGC and NP pathways are important in the pathophysilogy of glaucoma.
NO and NP receptors are important in the regulation of aqueous humor outflow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cGMP pathway plays an important role in IOP regulation and in the pathogenesis of glaucoma, and that it is a promising target for novel therapies and biomarkers.
soluble GC and membrane GC are key players in IOP regulation and that they are potential therapeutic targets for glaucoma.
NO and NPs are important regulators of IOP, and their receptors and downstream effectors are potential drug targets and biomarkers for the treatment of POAG.
